This week you learn how to **formulate hypotheses** and **test** them — focusing on tests of mean values with the **t-test**. Use the language toggle above to switch between R and Python.

<h3>Quiz 1: Formulating Hypotheses <span id="quiz-done-w7_q_hypotheses" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> You want to test whether the mean weight of 10 sampled chocolate bars differs from the expected 100 g. Is this a one-sample or two-sample test, and one- or two-sided?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy1" id="hy1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy1a">Two-sample, one-sided</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy1" id="hy1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy1b">One-sample, two-sided — comparing one sample's mean to a fixed target value, in either direction</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy1" id="hy1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy1c">Two-sample, two-sided</label></div>
    <div id="hy1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> To test whether males have a significantly <em>higher</em> mean weight than females, which <code>t.test()</code> alternative would you use?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy2" id="hy2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy2a"><code>alternative = "two.sided"</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy2" id="hy2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy2b"><code>alternative = "greater"</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy2" id="hy2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy2c"><code>alternative = "less"</code></label></div>
    <div id="hy2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does the significance level α represent?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy3" id="hy3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy3a">The probability that H1 is true</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy3" id="hy3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy3b">The false-positive rate: under H0, the proportion of tests that would (wrongly) detect a significant difference</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hy3" id="hy3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hy3c">The sample size needed for the test</label></div>
    <div id="hy3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkHypothesesQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="hypotheses-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Running &amp; Interpreting t-Tests <span id="quiz-done-w7_q_ttest" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> Why is the p-value of a one-tailed t-test always smaller than (or equal to) the p-value of the corresponding two-tailed test?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt1" id="tt1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt1a">The two-tailed p-value adds up the area in both tails of the t-distribution, so it is (about) twice the one-tailed p-value</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt1" id="tt1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt1b">One-tailed tests always use a different dataset</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt1" id="tt1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt1c">There is no relationship between the two p-values</label></div>
    <div id="tt1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> In the chocolate bar example (p-value = 0.052), what changes if you use α = 0.1 instead of α = 0.05?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt2" id="tt2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt2a">Nothing — the conclusion is always the same regardless of α</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt2" id="tt2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt2b">With α = 0.1, H0 can now be rejected since the p-value is below 0.1, even though it wasn't below 0.05</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt2" id="tt2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt2c">The p-value itself changes when you change α</label></div>
    <div id="tt2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> According to the exercise sheet, when should you choose your α value?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt3" id="tt3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt3a">After seeing the p-value, so you can pick whichever gives a significant result</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt3" id="tt3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt3b">Before running the test, together with formulating H0 and H1</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="tt3" id="tt3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="tt3c">α does not need to be decided in advance</label></div>
    <div id="tt3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkTtestQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="ttest-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Checking Normality <span id="quiz-done-w7_q_normality" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is a key requirement for a t-test to be valid?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm1" id="nm1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm1a">The data should be approximately normally distributed</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm1" id="nm1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm1b">The sample size must be exactly 10</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm1" id="nm1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm1c">There must be no missing values anywhere in the dataset</label></div>
    <div id="nm1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> How do you interpret <code>shapiro.test(x)$p.value</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm2" id="nm2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm2a">p-value ≥ 0.05 → data looks normally distributed; p-value &lt; 0.05 → data is not normally distributed</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm2" id="nm2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm2b">p-value ≥ 0.05 → data is NOT normal</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm2" id="nm2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm2c">The p-value has no meaning for the Shapiro-Wilk test</label></div>
    <div id="nm2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> If the Shapiro-Wilk test shows a variable is NOT normally distributed, what should you do instead of a t-test?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm3" id="nm3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm3a">Use a non-parametric test instead (e.g. the Wilcoxon test)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm3" id="nm3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm3b">Delete the dataset and collect new data</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nm3" id="nm3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nm3c">Run the t-test anyway, it makes no difference</label></div>
    <div id="nm3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkNormalityQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="normality-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 4: Understanding the Null Distribution <span id="quiz-done-w7_q_null" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> The exercise builds an empirical H0 distribution by repeatedly splitting the cohort into 2 <em>random</em> groups and computing the t-value each time. Why should there be no real difference between 2 random groups?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd1" id="nd1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd1a">Because random groups are drawn from the same overall population, so on average they shouldn't systematically differ</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd1" id="nd1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd1b">Because R always returns 0 for random samples</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd1" id="nd1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd1c">Because random groups are always exactly the same size</label></div>
    <div id="nd1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> The empirical H0 distribution of 10,000 random-split t-values closely matches which theoretical distribution?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd2" id="nd2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd2a">A t-distribution with df = number of patients − 2</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd2" id="nd2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd2b">A Poisson distribution</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd2" id="nd2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd2c">A uniform distribution</label></div>
    <div id="nd2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> A Verständnisfragen exercise samples two groups of 5 mice from the SAME population (true mean 100g) and runs both a 1-sample and 2-sample t-test. If H0 is rejected here, what kind of error occurred?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd3" id="nd3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd3a">A false positive (Type I error) — H0 was actually true, since both samples came from the same population</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd3" id="nd3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd3b">A false negative (Type II error)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nd3" id="nd3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nd3c">No error — rejecting H0 here is always correct</label></div>
    <div id="nd3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkNullQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="null-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

</div><!-- end .lang-r -->

<h3 style="margin-top:1.5rem;">Quiz 3: Checking Normality <span style="font-size:0.8rem;color:#7c9cef;font-weight:normal;">(scipy.stats.shapiro)</span></h3>
<div class="placeholder-card">
  <p style="color:#7c9cef;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:1rem;">🐍 Python Quiz — Coming Soon</p>
  <div style="opacity:0.65;">
    <p><strong>Preview Question:</strong> Which scipy.stats function performs a Shapiro-Wilk normality test?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" disabled=""><label class="form-check-label" style="color:#888;"><code>stats.shapiro()</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" disabled=""><label class="form-check-label" style="color:#888;"><code>stats.normaltest_only()</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" disabled=""><label class="form-check-label" style="color:#888;"><code>stats.ttest_ind()</code></label></div>
